story: NMFS issued the Office of Naval Research a Year 9 incidental harassment authorization covering the acoustic navigation grid that lets autonomous vehicles hold position under Arctic sea ice

claims.claim: The Federal Register notice published September 10th carries the action line Notice, issuance of incidental harassment authorization, so the authorization is decided and not proposed.
claims.verbatim: ACTION: Notice; issuance of incidental harassment authorization.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register via GPO govinfo, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: Confirmed independently in the federalregister.gov JSON API action field for document 2026-18459. Two routes agree.

claims.claim: NMFS states the authorization is effective from September 14th through September 13th, 2027.
claims.verbatim: DATES: This authorization is effective from September 14, 2026, through September 13, 2027.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register via GPO govinfo, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: Corroborated by the federalregister.gov JSON API effective_date field. One year to the day minus one, consistent with C47 on the statutory one year ceiling.

claims.claim: The notice carries the NOAA regulatory identifier RTID 0648-XF889, which is an identifier and not a measurement.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register via GPO govinfo, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: Appears in the header bracket line. Also returned as the docket id by the federalregister.gov JSON API. Identifier, not a quantity.

claims.claim: The issuance occupies Federal Register volume 91 pages 57547 through 57550, which makes 91 FR 57547 its citation address.
claims.verbatim:
[Federal Register Volume 91, Number 174 (Thursday, September 10, 2026)]
[Notices]
[Pages 57547-57550]
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register via GPO govinfo
claims.notes: Verified as the START page of a four page notice. Identifier, not a measurement. The JSON API independently reports volume 91, start page 57547.

claims.claim: The notice title names the action as Year 9 of the Office of Naval Research Arctic Research Activities in the Beaufort and Chukchi Seas.
claims.verbatim: Taking Marine Mammals Incidental to the Office of Naval Research's Arctic Research Activities in the Beaufort and Chukchi Seas (Year 9)
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register via GPO govinfo, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: Confirmed verbatim in the federalregister.gov JSON API title field as well.

claims.claim: The proposed notice says this authorization covers the ninth year of a larger project for which the Office of Naval Research obtained prior authorizations and renewals.
claims.verbatim: This proposed IHA would cover the ninth year of a larger project for which ONR obtained prior IHAs and renewal IHAs.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: The document says ninth year of the PROJECT, not the ninth authorization, because renewals are counted separately in the same sentence. Background document, incorporated by the September 10th issuance via C07.

claims.claim: The issuance states there are no changes to the specified activity, the species taken, the numbers or methods of take, or the mitigation and monitoring measures set out in the proposed notice.
claims.verbatim: There are no changes to the specified activity, the species taken, the proposed numbers, type, or methods of take, or the mitigation, monitoring, or reporting measures in the proposed IHA notice.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: LOAD BEARING for every claim sourced to the July 22nd proposed notice. This sentence is why the platform inventory and source levels in the proposed notice govern the issued authorization.

claims.claim: The proposed notice describes the activity as using acoustic sources and receivers to provide a means of performing under-ice navigation for autonomous underwater vehicles.
claims.value: under-ice navigation for autonomous underwater vehicles
claims.verbatim: utilizing acoustic sources and receivers to provide a means of performing under-ice navigation for autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs)
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: The purpose sentence, and the documents do say navigation in those words. Confirmed on the govinfo mirror. The word GPS never appears in either notice.

claims.claim: The proposed notice describes the activity as the development of a new system under the Arctic Mobile Observing System.
claims.verbatim: The proposed activity constitutes the development of a new system under AMOS involving very-low-, low-, and mid-frequency
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: The quoted fragment breaks mid sentence because the Federal Register plain text wraps it. The AMOS expansion is at C10.

claims.claim: The proposed notice places the Arctic Mobile Observing System inside the Navy Arctic and Global Prediction Program.
claims.verbatim: ONR's ARA include multiple scientific objectives that support the Arctic and Global Prediction Program, including Arctic Mobile Observing System (AMOS).
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: Gives the AMOS acronym expansion used in C09.

claims.claim: The study area is approximately 639,237 square kilometres.
claims.verbatim: The proposed Study Area is approximately 639,237 square kilometers (km\2\).
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: Square kilometres, not square miles. The backslash two is the Federal Register plain text rendering of a superscript. The document word is approximately and the deck keeps it.

claims.claim: The closest point of the study area to the Alaska coast is 204 kilometres, which the notice also gives as 110 nautical miles.
claims.verbatim: The closest point of the Study Area to the Alaska coast is 204 kilometers (km) (110 nautical miles).
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: Unit check passes, 110 nautical miles is 203.7 km, so the two figures in the document are consistent.

claims.claim: The activity would occur across the US Exclusive Economic Zone in the Beaufort and Chukchi seas, partially in the high seas north of Alaska and within part of the Canadian Exclusive Economic Zone.
claims.value: three jurisdictions, including part of the Canadian EEZ
claims.verbatim: The proposed activity would occur across the U.S. Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) in the Beaufort and Chukchi Seas, partially in the high seas north of Alaska, the global commons, and within a part of the Canadian EEZ
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: CORRECTION to the scout brief, which named two jurisdictions and omitted Canada. The document names three.

claims.claim: Up to six moorings described as fixed acoustic navigation sources transmitting at 900 Hz would be configured with active acoustic sources.
claims.verbatim: Up to six moorings (fixed acoustic navigation sources transmitting at 900 Hz) and two drifting ice gateway buoys (IGBs) would be configured with active acoustic sources and would operate for a period of 1 year.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: The document's own words are fixed acoustic navigation sources, a second independent support for the navigation purpose at C08. Count is up to six.

claims.claim: Two drifting ice gateway buoys would be configured with active acoustic sources.
claims.verbatim: Up to six moorings (fixed acoustic navigation sources transmitting at 900 Hz) and two drifting ice gateway buoys (IGBs) would be configured with active acoustic sources and would operate for a period of 1 year.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: The buoy count carries no up to, unlike the moorings. The source table row independently reads IGB (drifting) (2).

claims.claim: The moorings and ice gateway buoys would operate for a period of one year.
claims.verbatim: would be configured with active acoustic sources and would operate for a period of 1 year
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: The contrast the deck turns on, the ship is present 22 days and the sound sources run 12 months.

claims.claim: The 900 Hz navigation moorings transmit a 30 second pulse every four hours.
claims.verbatim: Mooring (6) WHOI Micro-modem Acoustic Navigation 900-950 Hz NTE 180 dB by 50 Hz Transmit every 4 (6) system design 30 sec limits pulse length.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: The Federal Register plain text interleaves the table columns, so the verbatim reads as scrambled word order. The same duty cycle appears cleanly in the ice gateway buoy row. Two rows agree.

claims.claim: The 900 to 950 Hz mooring sources carry a not to exceed source level of 180 dB set by system design limits.
claims.verbatim: Mooring (6) WHOI Micro-modem Acoustic Navigation 900-950 Hz NTE 180 dB by 50 Hz Transmit every 4 (6) system design 30 sec limits pulse length.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: The band is 900 to 950 Hz and not a single tone. NTE is not to exceed and the limit is a design limit rather than a measurement. Units belong to the column header at C19.

claims.claim: The source level column in the notice is headed with the reference convention dB re 1 microPascal at 1 m, so the numbers are source levels and not received levels.
claims.verbatim: Signal strength (dB re 1 [micro]Pa at 1 m)
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: The bracketed micro is the plain text substitution for the Greek mu. Any slide printing a bare dB is wrong.

claims.claim: Up to one REMUS 600 uncrewed undersea vehicle is covered, with an 8 to 14 kHz acoustic communications source at a not to exceed level of 185 dB.
claims.value: up to 1 REMUS 600 at 8 to 14 kHz
claims.verbatim: REMUS 600 UUV (up to 1) UUV/WHOI Micro-modem Acoustic 8-14 kHz NTE 185 dB by 5 kHz 10% average duty communications system design 4 sec limits cycle, with pulse length.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: CORRECTION to the scout brief, which paired 185 dB with 10 kHz. The table pairs 185 dB with the 8 to 14 kHz band.

claims.claim: The notice says REMUS use is not anticipated during the September 2026 cruise and is included only in case of future use inside the authorization period.
claims.value: not anticipated during the September 2026 cruise
claims.verbatim: REMUS use is not anticipated during the September 2026 cruise but is included in case of future use during the proposed IHA period.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: The deck must not say a REMUS 600 will be in the water this autumn. The authorization covers it, the cruise plan does not expect it.

claims.claim: Up to 20 Argo type autonomous profiling floats may be deployed in the central Beaufort Sea.
claims.verbatim: Up to 20 Argo-type autonomous profiling floats may be deployed in the central Beaufort Sea.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: Both up to and may be, so this is a ceiling and a permission, not a plan. The floats are passive profilers and are not listed among the acoustic sources.

claims.claim: Argo floats drift at 1,500 m depth and collect temperature and salinity profiles from 2,000 m to the sea surface once every 10 days.
claims.value: 1,500 m drift and 2,000 m profile every 10 days
claims.verbatim: Argo floats drift at 1,500 m depth and collect profiles of temperature and salinity from 2,000 m to the sea surface once every 10 days.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: The profile depth is deeper than the drift depth, which is how Argo floats work, so the magnitudes are internally consistent.

claims.claim: The notice says that in ice covered waters the gliders navigate by trilateration from moored acoustic sound sources, or by dead reckoning if the navigation signals are unavailable.
claims.value: trilateration from moored acoustic sound sources
claims.verbatim: When operating in ice-covered waters, gliders navigate by trilateration (the process of determining location by measurement of distances, using the geometry of circles, spheres, or triangles) from moored acoustic sound sources (or dead reckoning should navigation signals be unavailable).
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: The strongest single sentence in either document for the deck's argument. It is the mechanism, the moorings are the position fix, and navigation signals is the document's own phrase.

claims.claim: The gliders move at a speed of 0.25 metres per second, which the notice gives as approximately 23 km per day.
claims.verbatim: Gliders would collect data in the area of the shallow water sources and moored sources, moving at a speed of 0.25 meters per second, approximately 23 km per day.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: 0.25 m per second is 21.6 km per day, and the notice says approximately 23, so the document rounds generously. Keep the word approximately if both figures print.

claims.claim: The gliders are buoyancy driven, carry satellite modems for two way communication and can transit to depths of up to 1,000 m.
claims.verbatim: Gliders are buoyancy-driven, equipped with satellite modems providing two-way communication, and can transit to depths of up to 1,000 m.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: The satellite modem is the thing that stops working under ice, which is why the acoustic grid exists. That inference is the deck's and not the document's.

claims.claim: The very low frequency 35 Hz mooring source carries the highest not to exceed level in the table at 190 dB.
claims.verbatim: Mooring (2) * VLF Acoustic Navigation 35 Hz NTE 190 dB 6 Hz Up to 4 times per day, 10 minutes each.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: Footnoted with an asterisk and NOT in use in Year 9, see C29. A deck printing 190 dB without C29 beside it is misleading.

claims.claim: The notice states that no very low frequency 35 Hz sources would be used in Year 9 because of hardware availability.
claims.verbatim: No VLF sources (35 Hz) would be used in Year 9 due to hardware availability.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: Corroborated by two further sentences in the same document. This is also what makes the issuance's 185 dB ceiling consistent with the proposed notice's 190 dB table row, see C30.

claims.claim: The issuance states that source levels from acoustic sources would not exceed 185 dB by system design limits.
claims.verbatim: Since potentially impactful source levels from acoustic sources would not exceed 185 dB by system design limits, sound exposure levels would remain relatively low.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: TWO DOCUMENT RECONCILIATION. The July table lists a 190 dB VLF row, the September issuance caps the year at 185 dB. They do not conflict because the VLF sources are excluded from Year 9 at C29. The issuance governs. Take the units from C19.

claims.claim: The research cruise is planned for only 22 days in September and October, according to the issuance.
claims.verbatim: a research cruise that is planned for only 22 days in September-October 2026
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: Corroborated a second time in the same notice. NMFS uses the short duration as part of its reason for not requiring passive acoustic monitoring, so the figure is doing argumentative work.

claims.claim: The proposed notice gives the first cruise a planned start date of September 22nd.
claims.verbatim: the first cruise beginning September 22, 2026, and a potential second cruise occurring in summer 2027
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: Settles the scout disagreement. Two sanity checks pass, the date is after the September 14th effective date and a 22 day cruise from it ends in mid October. Hedge as planned, since this is a July statement about a cruise that has not sailed.

claims.claim: The issuance names the vessels as Research Vessel Sikuliaq, US Coast Guard Cutter HEALY, or another vessel.
claims.verbatim: The use of PAM on vessels (Research Vessel (R/V) Sikuliaq, U.S. Coast Guard Cutter HEALY, or another vessel)
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: The or another vessel clause matters and the deck can't state flatly which ship sails. No operator is named for Sikuliaq in either notice.

claims.claim: The proposed notice says the R/V Sikuliaq is not an icebreaking ship but an ice strengthened ship.
claims.verbatim: The R/V Sikuliaq is not an icebreaking ship but an ice strengthened ship
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: Relevant because icebreaking is a separately analyzed noise source in the same authorization, see C38.

claims.claim: A potential second cruise in summer 2027 may include up to 8 days of icebreaking activities.
claims.verbatim: a potential second cruise occurring in summer 2027, which may include up to 8 days of icebreaking activities.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: Needs softening, the words are potential and may include and up to. Summer 2027 falls inside the authorization period.

claims.claim: The Office of Naval Research request was for take of beluga whales and ringed seals by Level B harassment only.
claims.value: beluga whales and ringed seals, Level B only
claims.verbatim: ONR's request is for take of beluga whales and ringed seals by Level B harassment only.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: PRECISION WARNING. This describes the REQUEST. It becomes a statement about what was authorized only through C07, which says the species taken did not change. Safe phrasing is that the authorization covers Level B harassment of beluga whale and ringed seal. No take NUMBER is verifiable, see killed.

claims.claim: The issuance states that take by Level A harassment is neither anticipated nor authorized based on the nature of the planned activities.
claims.verbatim: Take by Level A harassment is neither anticipated nor authorized based on the nature of ONR's planned activities, even absent mitigation, and NMFS has appropriately considered this in its negligible impact analysis and determination.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: Level A is injury and Level B is behavioural disturbance under the Marine Mammal Protection Act. The deck should not let a reader think Level B means nothing happened.

claims.claim: NMFS did not authorize take by Level A harassment from icebreaking.
claims.verbatim: neither ONR nor NMFS expect these activities would result in Level A harassment of beluga whales or ringed seals and, therefore, NMFS did not authorize take by Level A harassment from icebreaking.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: A separate noise source with its own finding, analyzed even though the cruise plan does not currently include it.

claims.claim: The issuance states there is one marine mammal species with confirmed occurrence in the study area listed as threatened under the Endangered Species Act, the Arctic subspecies of ringed seal.
claims.verbatim: There is one marine mammal species (Arctic subspecies of ringed seal) with confirmed occurrence in the Study Area that is listed as threatened under the ESA.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: Threatened, not endangered. The deck must not upgrade the word. Corroborated by the proposed notice's stock table, which gives the Arctic ringed seal an ESA status code of T.

claims.claim: The NMFS Alaska Regional Office Biological Opinion relied on for this authorization was issued on September 13th, 2022 and concluded the action is not likely to jeopardize the continued existence of Arctic ringed seals.
claims.verbatim: The Biological Opinion concluded that the action is not likely to jeopardize the continued existence of Arctic ringed seals and is not likely to destroy or adversely modify Arctic ringed seal critical habitat.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: A separate verbatim sentence in the same notice reads NMFS AKR issued a Biological Opinion on September 13, 2022, under section 7 of the ESA, so a 2022 consultation is carrying Year 9.

claims.claim: The stock abundance estimate the notice gives for the Beaufort Sea beluga stock is 39,258, with a coefficient of variation of 0.229, from a 1992 survey.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: THIS IS AN ABUNDANCE ESTIMATE AND NOT AN AUTHORIZED TAKE. Never blend the two. Extracted from the same stock table by three independent routes, the plain text, the XML and the govinfo mirror, all agreeing. The 1992 survey year is part of the cell.

claims.claim: The stock abundance estimate the notice gives for the Eastern Chukchi beluga stock is 13,305, with a coefficient of variation of 0.51, from a 2017 survey.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: ABUNDANCE, NOT TAKE. The third value 8,875 is the minimum population estimate and is not a take number either. A coefficient of variation of 0.51 is high, so a slide using this should say the estimate is imprecise.

claims.claim: The notice lists the abundance of the Arctic ringed seal stock as undetermined, and its potential biological removal as undetermined.
claims.verbatim: Ringed seal (Arctic): Pusa hispida, Stock: Arctic, ESA/MMPA status: T, D, Y, Stock abundance: UND (UND, UND, 2013), PBR: UND, Annual M/SI: 6,459
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: The verbatim is a faithful reading of the stock table's cells with their field labels rather than a continuous sentence, so attribute it as the notice's stock table and do not quote it as prose. UND means undetermined in the table's own key. One of the two species in the authorization has no published abundance estimate and no calculated potential biological removal.

claims.claim: NMFS received three comment letters from private citizens during the 30 day public comment period.
claims.verbatim: During the 30-day public comment period, NMFS received three comment letters from private citizens.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: The letters are from private citizens, so the deck must not imply any tribal or co-management body commented.

claims.claim: Vessels must maintain a mitigation zone of 457 m around all observed cetaceans and 183 m around all other observed marine mammals.
claims.verbatim: vessels must avoid approaching marine mammals head-on and must maneuver to maintain a mitigation zone of 457 m around all observed cetaceans and 183 m around all other observed marine mammals
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: Magnitude check, 457 m is 500 yards and 183 m is 200 yards, customary NMFS standoff distances converted to metric. Observed is the operative word.

claims.claim: During deployment and recovery of moored and drifting acoustic sources the Office of Naval Research must implement a mitigation zone of 55 m around the deployed source.
claims.verbatim: during moored and drifting acoustic source deployment and recovery, ONR must implement a mitigation zone of 55 m around the deployed source
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: A second sentence in the same notice adds that deployment and recovery must cease if a marine mammal is visually detected within the zone. The zone applies during deployment only, not for the 12 months the source then transmits.

claims.claim: NMFS states that all authorizations it issues, whether an initial authorization or a renewal, are valid for a period of not more than one year.
claims.verbatim: All IHAs issued, whether an initial IHA or a renewal, are valid for a period of not more than 1 year
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: The structural fact behind the deck's thesis. A nine year programme runs on a one year instrument, which is why there are nine of these documents rather than one.

claims.claim: The only reference to subsistence in the issuance is the statutory standard NMFS must apply, which asks whether the taking will have an unmitigable adverse impact on the availability of the stock for subsistence uses where relevant.
claims.verbatim: NMFS shall issue an IHA if it finds that the taking will have a negligible impact on the species or stock(s) and will not have an unmitigable adverse impact on the availability of the species or stock(s) for taking for subsistence uses (where relevant).
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: Both notices were searched for subsistence, Inupiat, Alaska Native, co-management, tribal, hunt and harvest. This boilerplate recitation of the section 101(a)(5)(D) standard, with its qualifier where relevant, is the only hit in either document. The deck may say the documents do not discuss subsistence use beyond the statutory test. It can't say the notices weigh it.

claims.claim: The issuance says modeling did not predict Level A take of beluga whale because the acoustic sources are continuous with a low duty cycle and a relatively short ping duration of 4 to 30 seconds.
claims.verbatim: for beluga whale, modeling did not predict take by Level A harassment given that the acoustic sources are continuous with a low duty cycle and relatively short ping duration (4-30 seconds)
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: Cross check passes against the source table. The 4 second figure is the REMUS pulse length at C20 and the 30 second figure is the mooring and buoy pulse length at C17, so the issuance's range matches the proposed notice at both ends.

claims.claim: The issuance states the estimated range to temporary hearing threshold shift is less than 15 m and that the range to auditory injury would be smaller still.
claims.verbatim: Further, the estimated range to TTS is <15 m (see table 5 of the notice of proposed IHA (91 FR 46055, July 22, 2026)), and the range to AUD INJ would be even smaller.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: In context the sentence is about ringed seals. TTS is temporary threshold shift and AUD INJ is auditory injury. A 15 m injury range beside the 55 m deployment zone at C46 is internally coherent. It is a modeled range, so hedge with estimated.

claims.claim: The issuance was signed by Kimberly Damon-Randall, Director of the NMFS Office of Protected Resources, and dated September 4th, then filed on September 9th.
claims.verbatim:
Dated: September 4, 2026.
Kimberly Damon-Randall,
Director, Office of Protected Resources, National Marine Fisheries Service.
[FR Doc. 2026-18459 Filed 9-9-26; 8:45 am]
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register via GPO govinfo, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: Date chain is coherent, signed September 4th, filed September 9th at 8.45 am, published September 10th, effective September 14th.

claims.claim: The proposed notice was published on July 22nd at 91 FR 46055 and the issuance cites it as the document it incorporates.
claims.verbatim: On July 22, 2026, a notice of NMFS' proposal to issue an IHA to ONR for take of marine mammals incidental to ARA in the Beaufort and Chukchi Seas was published in the Federal Register (91 FR 46055).
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register plain text, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: An identifier, not a measurement. This claim is the audit trail for the two document structure. The issuance cites the proposed notice three separate times.

claims.claim: The proposed notice action line invited comment on the proposed authorization and on a possible renewal of it.
claims.verbatim: ACTION: Notice; proposed incidental harassment authorization; request for comments on proposed authorization and possible renewal.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Register via GPO govinfo, NOAA National Marine Fisheries Service
claims.notes: Supports C47 and the one year at a time thesis. The renewal for Year 10 is already inside the comment scope of the Year 9 proposal.

killed.claim: The authorization permits a specific number of Level B harassment takes of beluga whale and ringed seal.
killed.why: FETCH FAILURE CONFIRMED ACROSS FOUR ROUTES, not a false claim. The federalregister.gov plain text of the proposed notice, its full text XML, the govinfo HTML mirror and the plain text of the issuance all return the surrounding prose and the stock table but no take table, and the issuance contains no take numbers at all because it incorporates them by reference. Scout E was right and Scout C never had take numbers. No take figure may appear on any slide. Remedy if wanted later, retrieve table 6 or 7 of 91 FR 46055 from the printed PDF at govinfo rather than the HTML or XML.

killed.claim: Authorized take equals or can be inferred from the beluga abundance estimates of 39,258 and 13,305.
killed.why: Category error. An abundance estimate is a population size and an authorized take is a permitted number of harassment events. The two are unrelated in magnitude and the deck must never present one as the other. C41 and C42 carry this warning in their notes.

killed.claim: R/V Sikuliaq is operated by the University of Alaska Fairbanks, which gives the story its Alaska institutional hook.
killed.why: NOT IN EITHER NOTICE and no primary source reachable today. Both documents were searched for Sikuliaq and four sentences came back, none naming an owner or operator. Five candidate primary pages were tried, uaf.edu/cfos/research/sikuliaq 404, sikuliaq.alaska.edu root and /about both 503, two nsf.gov paths 404, unols.org 404 on three URL forms. The only page that loaded was Wikipedia, which this publication does not cite for an institutional fact. The deck may say the notice names R/V Sikuliaq and must not name an operator. Remedy, retry sikuliaq.alaska.edu when the 503 clears.

killed.claim: The acoustic navigation grid exists because GPS does not reach under Arctic sea ice.
killed.why: TRUE AS PHYSICS, ABSENT AS DOCUMENT LANGUAGE. Neither notice contains the string GPS or Global Positioning anywhere. This is the deck's own gloss and must be written as the deck's explanation, never attributed to NMFS or the Navy. The document-supported substitutes are C25, which says the gliders navigate by trilateration from moored acoustic sound sources or by dead reckoning should navigation signals be unavailable, and C27, which says the gliders rely on satellite modems.

killed.claim: The authorization licenses noise in water that beluga, ringed seal and Inupiat hunters share.
killed.why: THE SUBSISTENCE HALF IS UNSOURCED IN THE RECORD. The beluga and ringed seal half is verified at C36 and C39. The words Inupiat, Alaska Native, tribal, hunt, hunter, harvest and co-management appear nowhere in either notice, and the sole subsistence reference is the statutory test at C48. The study area's closest approach to the Alaska coast is 204 km per C12, which the deck has to reckon with before asserting shared use. This framing is removed from the deck rather than softened, and the thesis was rewritten around what the permit KNOWS instead.

killed.claim: Source levels are 180 dB at 900 Hz, 185 dB at 10 kHz and 190 dB for 35 Hz VLF sources.
killed.why: PARTLY WRONG AS STATED. The 185 dB row is the 8 to 14 kHz band and not 10 kHz, see C20. The 190 dB VLF row is real at C28 but those sources are not in use in Year 9 per C29, and the issuance caps the year at 185 dB per C30. The bare unit dB is also wrong throughout, the convention is dB re 1 microPascal at 1 m, see C19.

killed.claim: A REMUS 600 uncrewed undersea vehicle will operate in the Beaufort Sea during the autumn cruise.
killed.why: CONTRADICTED BY THE DOCUMENT at C21. The authorization covers up to one REMUS 600, which is a permission and not a plan, and the notice says REMUS use is not anticipated during the September 2026 cruise. A slide showing a REMUS in the water this autumn would be false.

killed.claim: The study area lies entirely within the US Exclusive Economic Zone, partially in the high seas.
killed.why: INCOMPLETE, corrected at C13. The notice names the US EEZ, the high seas north of Alaska described as the global commons, AND a part of the Canadian EEZ. Dropping Canada understates the jurisdictional reach, which is one of the permit's more interesting features.

killed.claim: The September 10th issuance notice describes the activity purpose as under-ice navigation.
killed.why: WRONG DOCUMENT. The issuance was searched for navigation, Arctic Mobile Observing System and AMOS and contains none of the three. The purpose language lives only in the July 22nd proposed notice at C08, which the issuance incorporates via C07. The deck attributes the navigation purpose to the July notice and not to the issuance.

killed.claim: A duplicate trilateration claim was returned as C24 with a mistyped source URL.
killed.why: DROPPED FROM THE RECORD RATHER THAN REPAIRED. The fact-checker returned the trilateration sentence twice, once at C24 with a source_url containing a drafting typo and a self-flagged confidence of 0.5, and once at C25 with the correct URL. C25 is kept and C24 is removed, because a published verification record is what the source archive is built from and a broken link in it is a defect whether or not the quote is right.
